summary: Lynn Thomas works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Lancaster University (BA, MA) and the University of Oxford (D.Phil, 1987). Her career includes a post as lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton, attested in 1997.

Léon Feer was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Lycée Pierre-Corneille and École des Langues Orientales under Etienne Marc Quatremère and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at INALCO, Collège de France, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Léon Vandermeersch was a Sinologist and philosopher who studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held posts at the National Museum of Vietnamese History, Aix-Marseille University, Paris Diderot, EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and EFEO.

Lê Mạnh Thát is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He earned a BA at the University of Saigon (~1962–1965) and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1974), later working at Vạn Hạnh University (~1974–1975).

M. A. Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and held a professorship in Sanskrit at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983).
M. Athar Ali was a historian who studied at Aligarh Muslim University from circa 1948 to 1953. He subsequently worked as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from circa 1953 to 1990.

M. D. Balasubrahmanyam is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1969. He held posts at Pune University (attested 1967), Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, and Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan (attested 1973).

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, University of Madras, and University College London. He served as Professor of History and Dean of Arts at the University of Mysore, and headed Maharaja's College department in 1932.

M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She held posts at Newnham College, Murray Edwards College, King's College London (Professor, 1990–2014), and University College London (~2014).

M. N. Srinivas was a sociologist and Indologist educated at Mysore, Mumbai, and Oxford under M. H. Krishna, G. S. Ghurye, Radcliffe-Brown, and Evans-Pritchard. He held posts at Oxford, Baroda, Delhi, All Souls College, ISEC, and NIAS.

M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and he served as a professor at the University of Calicut.

M. S. A. Rao was a sociologist who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (~1959–1985), Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, and as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.
M. Shinoda is a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami and attended Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design (~1995–1998).

M. Yamunacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.

Mabel Haynes Bode was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Bern, UCL, Collège de France, Sorbonne, EPHE, and Pisa. She held lecturing posts in Pali at University College London (1909, 1911–1917) and SOAS (~1917–1922).

Madeleine Biardeau was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres and the University of Kerala under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri, and was Professor of Indian Religions at EPHE (~1956–1989).
Madhav Krishna Sharma is an Indologist who studied as a pupil under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1952, he held a post as Inspector in the Department of Sanskrit Education, Rajasthan.

Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He held a professorial post at the University of Michigan, with his appointments there attested in 1976, 1997, and from 2006 to 2009.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. In 2012, she held attested posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.
